title: Per-request KPI sampler and trace-correlation proxy for inference nodes
creator: Aria Kim
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight sampling proxy that runs adjacent to inference workers (edge and dedicated nodes) to capture a small, deterministic fraction of per-request KPI envelopes and attach trace identifiers so downstream metric pipelines can produce per-request latency/error histograms correlated with traces. This avoids full-traffic high-cardinality ingestion while preserving causal linkage for debugging regressions.

Scope:
- Implement an in-process/sidecar proxy that listens for a telemetry POST (OTLP metrics/span metadata or a compact KPI envelope) and forwards sampled envelopes to the central telemetry gateway.
- Inject or propagate a stable trace_id/request_id pair (prefer W3C traceparent + service-specific request id) into the KPI envelope so the metric pipeline can join traces and metrics for a sampled request.
- Sampling strategy: deterministic hashing by tenant+route with per-tenant overrides, and a burst-protection reservoir to capture tails during incident windows. Configurable percent and absolute rate.
- Compatibility: support both OTLP proto over gRPC and a compact JSON KPI-envelope for low-overhead edge SDKs; output to existing OTLP ingress and Prometheus pushgateway adapters.
- Schema: minimal KPI envelope fields: timestamp, request_id, traceparent, model, route, shard_latency_ms, decode_tokens, top_err_code (if any), kv_cache_hit (bool), node_id. Add proto v1->v2 migration headers for compatibility.
- Observability: dashboards and alerting hooks to track sampler health (queue depth, drop rate, last-forwarded-ts) and sampling coverage percent by tenant/route.

Success criteria:
1) End-to-end linkage: sampled KPI envelopes are joinable with traces in the trace viewer within 5s of ingestion.
2) Low overhead: CPU < 0.5% and p50 latency added by proxy < 1ms on a 16-core inference node at 75% load.
3) Effective tail capture: during a synthetic incident test the reservoir increases sampled tail coverage by >=5x for top 0.1% latency requests.

Implementation notes / trade-offs considered:
- Sidecar vs in-process: start with a sidecar for safer rollout; plan an optional in-process SDK embedding for microsecond-sensitive paths.
- Deterministic hashing avoids feedback loops in sampling when autoscaling changes node counts. Downside: may under-sample rare transient errors; reservoir sampling partially mitigates this.
- Avoid sending full request payloads (promote PII safety); only send identifiers and derived KPIs. Full payloads remain available via trace ID lookups when requested with proper access control.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch + unit/integration tests (OTLP/JSON ingest, trace propagation).
2) Canary on internal staging inference fleet (5% of traffic) with detailed dashboards.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% for non-sensitive tenants; for sensitive/regulated tenants sampler defaults to off until opt-in.

Artifacts & links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/KPI+Sampler+Design  ; GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/2389 ; Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/kpi-sampler-coverage

Operational runbook snippet: if forward error rate > 1% for 5m, automatically reduce sampling percent by 4x and page telemetry-oncall. If reservoir fill time exceeds 2m, drop non-reservoir low-priority envelopes and emit backpressure metric.
